paper.title: Multiple nodal superconducting phases and order-parameter evolution in pressurized UTe2

claims: Zero-bias conductance peaks from zero-energy Andreev bound states on the (0 0 1) surface show that the UTe2 order parameter has a pz component and nodes.
Extended BTK fits favour the B2u or B3u representation for both ambient and pressurized UTe2, with Au and B1u disfavoured.
At ambient pressure (SC1) the px(y) component dominates, with Δz/Δx(y) of about 0.57 across three samples.
The ratio ⟨Δz⟩/⟨Δx(y)⟩ distinguishes the pressure-induced phases: the pz weight rises abruptly from SC1 to SC3, reaching about 1.3 at 1.2 GPa.
A minimum in the ratio versus temperature marks the SC2 to SC3 transition, which may be a change from B2u to B3u.
summary: Point-contact spectroscopy on the (0 0 1) surface of UTe2 from ambient pressure to 1.4 GPa shows a zero-bias conductance peak that develops side dips above about 0.3 GPa. Fitting the spectra with an extended BTK model for spin-triplet pairing, the authors favour B2u or B3u and use the ratio of pz to px(y) gap amplitudes to distinguish the SC1, SC2 and SC3 phases.

issues.claim: Side dips as evidence of pz dominance in SC2/SC3
issues.issue: The side dips that appear under pressure, and the flat-topped 1.4 GPa spectrum, look like the critical-current or thermal-regime signature of a point contact, possibly from several parallel nano-contacts. The heating argument is qualitative and made only at ambient pressure, where there are no dips, and the paper gives no junction resistance, contact size, mean-free-path comparison or dI/dV measurement scheme. Without this the dips cannot be attributed to bulk-continuum depletion by surface Andreev bound states.

evidence.quote: As we will further explain below, the appearance of these side dips suggests that these ZBCPs are intrinsic and associated with the formation of ZABS.

issues.fix: Report R_N(p, T) for each spectrum with a Wexler-type regime analysis and describe the dI/dV scheme; show how the dip position evolves with temperature and field at 0.6 to 1.4 GPa and whether it scales with R_N or series resistance across contacts; state whether the 1.4 GPa spectrum is in the thermal regime.
issues.fix_scoped: As we will further explain below, these side dips are consistent with the formation of ZABS, although a critical-current origin in the thermal regime has not yet been excluded for the pressurized junction.

issues.claim: Δz/Δx(y) as a measure of pairing weights; BCS violation
issues.issue: The fitted gaps (about 1.15 meV at ambient pressure with Tc of 2.1 K, up to 1.6 meV at 1.2 GPa) give 2Δ/kBTc of about 12 to 13, far above the few tenths of a meV reported by other probes. Such a ratio is not a signature of unconventional pairing; it suggests the fitted Δ absorbs other energy scales such as critical-current structure, spreading resistance, broadening or parallel contacts. If so, Δx and Δz are not physical gap amplitudes and their ratio may not measure the pairing weights.

evidence.quote: they both strongly violate the BCS’s prediction, which again demonstrates the unconventional nature of SC in UTe2.

issues.fix: Compare the fitted Δ(T→0) with Tc, literature gaps and observed ZBCP widths; correct for series resistance and show the voltage scale does not depend on R_N; explain why the fitted Δ is a gap; and show whether the ratio survives when the absolute gap is constrained to physically reasonable values.
issues.fix_scoped: The temperature dependence of Δx(y) and Δz of sample S1 at ambient pressure is presented in Fig. S2(c); their magnitudes exceed the weak-coupling BCS value by a factor of about four, so they are treated here as effective fit parameters rather than as superconducting gap amplitudes.

The authors' own simulations show side dips appear only for large Z and small Γ, so the onset of dips above 0.3 GPa and the change in the ratio cannot be separated from changes in the junction.

issues.fix_scoped: A reproducible ZBCP is observed on the (0 0 1) surface of three samples at ambient pressure; in the single junction measured under pressure, the ZBCP profile changes strongly with pressure, with side dips appearing above 0.3 GPa, which we tentatively attribute to nodal gap structure since the junction parameters also changed during the pressure run.

issues.issue: Au is excluded using only an isotropic simulation with Γ = 0.01 meV, while realistic Γ and unequal components would wash out the peak splitting; B1u is excluded only by absent side dips, which S1 and S2 also lack at ambient pressure. issues.claim: Meaning of the extracted gap ratio
issues.issue: The model assumes a single spherical Fermi surface with linear-in-k p-wave basis functions, while UTe2 has quasi-2D cylindrical sheets along kz with small, strongly k-dependent vz. The weighting of channels, and so the ratio Δz/Δx(y), then depends on normalization and basis, and the step-function gap neglects pair breaking at the (001) surface for the sign-changing pz component.

evidence.quote: In accordance with the experimental setup, we consider a planar NM-SC junction whose interface is perpendicular to the crystallographic c-axis of UTe2.

issues.fix: Re-run the analysis with a quasi-2D cylindrical or tight-binding Fermi surface, or at minimum discuss how it would alter the simulated spectra; report how the ratio and the Au/B2u discrimination change; discuss the non-self-consistent gap treatment.

demo.note: This sample is a published paper whose referee reports are public, so the dashboard can show which of the referees' concerns the review anticipated.

referee_concerns.summary: The analysis assumes triplet p-wave BTK throughout without showing that singlet s- or d-wave pairing cannot explain the spectra.
The three ambient-pressure samples give visibly different spectra, which needs explaining.
The broad, flat-topped 1.4 GPa spectrum is neither fitted nor physically interpreted; does it mean a larger gap?
Can PCS test the suggested link between the field-induced and pressure-induced SC2 phases?
Can the data or fits say whether SC2 or SC3 is chiral or breaks time-reversal symmetry?
The Kondo-related Fano background may distort the normalized superconducting spectra.
The (001) geometry cannot separate B2u from B3u, so the order parameter is not pinned down.
Typos: 'spits', 'Supplementray', 'differentiate conductance'.
The side dips under pressure may come from a cleaner contact (Gamma falls to 0.10 meV), as S3 already shows side structure at 0 GPa, rather than from a change in the gap ratio.
All pressure data come from one contact on sample S1; another pressurized contact, re-contacting or pressure cycling is needed.
The high-pressure side dips could be critical-current artifacts; field-dependent spectra at 0.6 or 0.8 GPa are needed.
Ruling out B1u rests on an idealized single-band specular model that drops the symmetry-allowed kx ky kz term, which does change sign under kz to -kz and is not small on UTe2's Fermi surface.
Fully gapped Au pairing, favoured by Knight shift and thermal conductivity, is dismissed qualitatively; quantitative Au fits, including multiband sensitivity and large Gamma, are needed.
The abstract overstates the identification of B2u or B3u given Au, B1u and B2u/B3u ambiguities.
The extended BTK fits have many free parameters and their uniqueness is not shown.
Pressure inhomogeneity, one proposed origin of the 1.0 to 1.2 GPa double dip, is implausible in Daphne 7373.
The linear superposition model of Eq. (2) ignores interband coupling and its limits are not discussed.
The multichannel model at high pressure adds fit parameters that improve fits without necessarily carrying information.
The fitted broadening Gamma is nearly temperature independent, which is atypical.
The abstract's link to non-Abelian zero modes for quantum computation contradicts the nodal state the paper claims.
The introduction wrongly equates spin-singlet with conventional superconductivity.
The claim of many controversies cites only one compound.
No evidence is given that the polished (001) contacts are ballistic, which the BTK analysis requires.
It is unclear whether RRR 410 refers to the authors' crystals or only to cited work.
Table S1 labels and the Delta_z/Delta_x(y) conclusions in the text appear inconsistent.
A B2u to B3u switch at the SC2-SC3 boundary is inconsistent with Landau free-energy arguments.
The nodal claim is not directly supported by PCS and depends on the fitting model.
Fig. 1b should label the k directions.
The Fig. 1c condition I perpendicular to q_N is stated too narrowly.
Fig. 4 simulations use a lower temperature than the experiment.
A claim in the SI Highlights about prior work lacks a citation.
Fitted gaps far exceed the STM gap and the BCS value, which may mean BTK does not apply.
The isotropic single-band free-electron model ignores anisotropic Fermi velocities, multiple bands, heavy-fermion character and SOC, which could change Delta_x versus Delta_z.
